_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for SHW retrospectives (retro/build_shw.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2008 were accepted during the session on their release days, and the outlook 8-K of 2008-03-24 before the open. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it; a next-quarter guide while its quarter is unreported) and the latest declared dividend. Sherwin-Williams' fiscal year is the calendar year. Each release and outlook 8-K guides the next quarter and the year: diluted EPS ranges in numbers; net sales in numbers in the Q2 and Q3 2007 releases, otherwise in words ('fy_words', 'words': shown, no field). Values are as reported; a vintage takes each year from the latest filing that reports it (eps_sources, revenue_sources, shares_sources), and the company's 2000 figure excluding the impairment replaces GAAP (the 'normalization' says which). A print's growth and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', thousands; the builder re-derives and checks them): the year-ago quarter is the one the same release shows; comparable-store sales, Consumer Group sales growth and the currency effect are the release's stated figures. rule_t holds the annual values behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.

rule_t._doc: Rule T values behind the engine's signal thresholds (retro/README.md, 'SHW'): the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04, is 1997-2006. Each change comes from the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years: net sales, gross profit (net sales less cost of goods sold) and income before income taxes from its statements of consolidated income; Consumer segment net external sales from its segment tables (in millions in the five-year tables, in thousands where the same filing's MD&A table gives them); comparable-store sales as each 10-K states them (no filing states 1997's, so that signal has the nine years 1998-2006: rule T takes the annual values the filings report). Everything as reported, seams included (the 1997 Thompson Minwax acquisition, the FY2002 10-K's restatement of Consumer segment sales for 2000-2001, the 2006 realignment into the Paint Stores, Consumer and Global Groups), except 2000's income before income taxes, which is the company's figure excluding the $352,040K impairment charge (the FY2002 10-K's $495,446K; the LOW rule).
